summary.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 81.7% YoY to INR747.6 crore with EBITDA margin near 20%; FY26 term debt fully repaid.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR747.6 crore (+81.7% YoY, +58.5% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR149.6 crore (19.99% margin vs 16.7% a year earlier) and PAT of INR102.2 crore (+128.9% YoY). Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR1,851.5 crore (+48.8%), EBITDA INR344.4 crore (18.6% margin, +300 bps) and PAT INR201.8 crore (+70.1%). All term loans were repaid by 31 March 2026, and the Vadod unit 4 received PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV on 2 April 2026. Management flagged a planned inventory drawdown ahead of April maintenance shutdowns and a mineral oil shortage in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: +117.9% YoY; margin vs 16.7% in Q4 FY25
up from INR910 crore; mainly non-fund based

segments.name: Vadod unit 4 (new)
segments.commentary: Produced 6,960 MVA in about seven months from July 2025 start, roughly 39% of 30,000 MVA nameplate; dispatched about 15 transformers per month in each of the last three months of FY26. Investment about INR200 crore; management cites Vadod revenue of about INR495 crore in first seven months.

segments.name: Atlanta Trafo unit 5 (Ankhi)
segments.commentary: Contributed 580 MVA in about three months during Q3 FY26; focused on 765 kV class prototype.

segments.name: Legacy units (Anand and Bengaluru, three units)
segments.commentary: Ran at very high utilisation through FY26. Total FY26 output across five units was 22,943 MVA.

segments.name: 220 kV and above mix
segments.commentary: 220 kV class constitutes nearly 52% of revenue; management says margins on 220 kV and below are expected to remain stable.

guidance_outlook: Vadod utilisation expected at about 65% in FY27 and 100% in FY28; mainstream 400 kV production from FY28 would take capacity to 30,000 MVA.
Management targets about 40% revenue CAGR for the next three years; margins guided to stay stable, within an 18-20% band.
Net working capital days expected to rise to around 80-90 in FY27 and FY28 as higher-kV mix grows.
400/765 kV products expected to carry about 200 bps higher margin, but R&D, technical tie-up and type-testing costs will offset this near term.
Exports targeted at 15% of total revenue within three years; first export breakthrough expected in FY27, with execution in FY28.
Unit 6 (IDT, about 5,000 MVA, Vadod adjacent) targeted for operation before December 2026; tank and radiator backward integration (INR170-180 crore) to start in FY27, near Vadod.
capex_capacity: Unit 6 inverter duty transformer facility: about INR65 crore capex, about 5,000 MVA, adjacent to Vadod, targeted operational before end of calendar 2026.
Tank and radiator backward integration: INR170-180 crore capex, robotic, to commence in FY27 near Vadod; benefits expected from FY28.
Capex funded through internal accruals; board has approved a term loan facility that may be drawn if required, with intent to repay in the following year.
Vadod PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV received 2 April 2026, subject to short circuit test and final qualifying requirements; short circuit test transformer to be sent in the coming quarter.
Plans to merge Atlanta Trafo Limited into Atlanta Electricals Limited to be initiated shortly.
demand_pricing: Around 75% of the unexecuted order book is under price variation clause; state utility boards form 60-75% of orders recently, and private long-horizon orders increasingly carry price variation too.
Management says commodity cost increases (copper, aluminium, crude-linked components) are largely passed through; management reports no hit taken in Q4.
Supply constraints persist for OIP bushings; conductor supply improving. Mineral oil shortage in Q4 due to West Asia conflict was managed by prioritising green (ester oil) transformers.
Realisation per MVA rose above INR8 lakh; management expects it to fall as 400/765 kV units (typically 500 MVA) enter.
Three new demand verticals cited: BESS, data centres and renewables. No data centre order in the book yet; BESS orders are in the order book. HVDC not targeted for now.
Competitive landscape: management argues demand will exceed supply for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable given the EHV mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins on 220 kV and below are stable; the gain came from 220 kV scale-up. Margins expected to stay stable going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How is realisation rising from INR7 to INR8 lakh per MVA if EHV will reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-MVA pricing is linked to commodity prices (steel, copper, oil) via customer contracts, so it rises with commodities; it will fall as 500 MVA class 400/765 kV units come in.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for 765 kV and tank/radiator capex and debt drawdown?
qa_highlights.answer: 765 kV is at marketing stage with prototyping this year; orders won this year would be invoiced next year. Tank and radiator facility starts this FY with benefits next year; term loan may be drawn if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Vadod utilisation trajectory and revenue from higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation 39% in FY26, 65% in FY27, 100% in FY28; most FY27 output still 220 kV with some 400 kV.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin gap between 400 kV and 220 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 400/765 kV margins about 200 bps higher; no 400 kV revenue yet.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre order share and HVDC plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No data centre order in the book; management is in talks with customers. HVDC not targeted until 400/765 kV prototypes are validated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of order book on price variation and any Q4 commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the INR2,493 crore order book has price variation; no commodity hit in Q4, and no hit is expected in Q1 as far as management can see.

qa_highlights.question: Margin accretion from backward integration and higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration is for supply chain control and quality, not margin; margins expected to remain fairly stable after 400/765 kV development costs.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: 220 kV and below takes 12-18 months; 80-85% of the current order book executes in FY27. Small 400 kV portion delivers from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Transformer demand thumb rule per GW and BESS opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 8-11x transformer capacity per GW generation, expected to tilt higher with BESS; BESS sizing not quantified for Atlanta.

risks_watch: Commodity and input costs: copper, oil and small components (gaskets, paints) are rising; OIP bushing supply is tight.
Working capital will rise to around 80-90 days in FY27-28, which could absorb cash flow.
Execution risk on 400 kV short circuit test, 765 kV tech tie-up (targeted in about two months) and Vadod utilisation ramp to 65%.
Export ramp (15% of revenue target) and first export orders are not yet quantified.
Unit 6 IDT and tank/radiator commissioning timelines (end-CY26 and FY27) could slip.
Management avoided committing to the timing of the short circuit test.
Margins are guided flat, so the margin upside from EHV has not been quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, capacity and PGCIL approval, with a clear 40% CAGR ambition. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on margin upside, 765 kV timing, export markets and data centre sizing, citing prototype-first discipline.
key_quotes: This margin expansion is structural in nature, driven by operating leverage from higher volumes, a richer product mix tilting towards 220KV class, which now constitutes nearly 52% of our revenue, and improved procurement efficiency on key input materials.
The single biggest operation milestone in the FY26 is the PGCIL approval for the manufacturing of transformers up to 400KV at our unit four, which is Vadod facility.
Team Atlanta booked INR2,507 crores of new order during FY26, which elevated our unexecuted order book on 31st March 2026 to INR2,493 crores.
